comments.why_zh: 关于 Bezier curves 及其导数的有趣视频
comments.quote_zh: 来源是一个关于 bezier curves 的非常有趣的视频，我强烈推荐
comments.text_zh: Bezier curves。三次 bezier curves（通常是最常见的类型）由三次多项式 x(t) 和 y(t) 表示（或者只用一个多项式 P(t)，其中系数是向量）。一阶导数给出切线和法线。二阶导数给出随着 t 增大法线将逐渐变成的方向。三阶导数给出这种变化的变化（四阶导数为零）。曲率也由一阶和二阶导数计算：K = det(P', P'')/||P'||^3。其他类型的 bezier curves 也类似。在二次型中，一阶和二阶导数分别是法线和法线的变化，但三阶导数为零。在更高次多项式的 bezier curves 中，三阶导数会随时间变化，因为四阶导数非零，以此类推。来源是一个关于 bezier curves 的非常有趣的视频，我强烈推荐：[VIDEO] 。
comments.text: Bezier curves. Cubic bezier curves (generally the most common type) are represented by cubic polynomials x(t) and y(t) (or just one polynomial P(t) where the coefficients are vectors). The first derivative gives you the tangent and normal. The second derivative gives you the direction the normal will gradually become as t increases. The third derivative gives you the change in this change (the fourth derivative is zero). Curvature is also computed from the first and second derivatives: K = det(P', P'')/||P'||^3 Other kinds of bezier curves are similar. In quadratic ones the first and second derivatives are normal and normal change but the third derivative is zero. In higher-polynomial bezier curves the third derivative changes over time as the fourth is non-zero, and so on. Source is a really interesting video on bezier curves which I highly recommend: [VIDEO] .

comments.author: an1sotropy
comments.story_title: Ask HN: Why are quadratic Bezier curves described so obtusely?
comments.why_zh: 精彩地解释并图示了 Bezier curves
comments.quote_zh: 他们在解释和图示方面做得非常漂亮。
comments.text_zh: 三次 Beziers 并不是 3D 的。你正在用来读这段话的字体（尤其是如果你把它打印出来）很有可能用一连串三次 Beziers 来定义这些（2D）字母的轮廓。很多 2D 计算机图形使用三次 Beziers，因为它们大致平衡了两方面的需求：既有很多自由度来表达，又不会复杂到求值很痛苦。而定义二次 Bezier 的控制点可以位于任意维度，包括 3 维，甚至 1 维，这对绘制基函数很有用。你所处的位置会塑造你理解事物的方式。当你学会从不同视角看待 Bézier curves 时，你当前这个特定的物理视角会和其他视角共存。学数学一直是这样。顺便说一句，那种迷失方向的感觉是值得珍惜的；你不会一直拥有它。我的直觉是，这个视频 [VIDEO] 出自一个学习 Bézier curves 的路径并不传统的人之手，但他们在解释和图示方面做得非常漂亮。它让我看到，我也还有更多东西要学。
comments.text: It is not the case that cubic Beziers are 3D. There’s a good chance that the font you’re using to read this (especially if you print it out) defines the outline of (2D) letters with a sequence of cubic Beziers. Lots of 2D computer graphics uses cubic Beziers because they ~balance the needs of having lots of DOF for expressivity, while not being so complicated that they’re a pain to evaluate. And the control points that define a quadratic Bezier could be in any dimension, including 3, or even 1, which is good for plotting the basis functions. Where you are shapes how you make sense of things. As you learn to see Bézier curves from different viewpoints, the particular physical viewpoint you have now will coexist with others. It’s always that way learning math. That feeling of being disoriented is something to treasure, btw; you won’t always have it. My hunch is that this video [VIDEO] comes from someone who’s path through learning Bézier curves was non-traditional, but they do a beautiful job of explaining and illustrating things. It showed me that I have more to learn too.
